READING PASSAGE 2

You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 14–26, which are based on Reading Passage 2 below.

Antarctic research

Thirteen nations took part in the recent International Polar Year

A New Zealand's contribution to International Polar Year was a 52-day voyage by the ship Tangaroa in order to conduct research in Antarctica's Ross Sea. Lead scientist Mary Livingston emphasises just what a multi-faceted expedition this was, bringing together zoologists, oceanographers, meteorologists and other scientists from the Ministry of Fisheries, the National Institute for Water and Atmospheric Research, the National Museum and various universities, to study life beneath the seas of Antarctica. Competition for berths – the ship can carry 44 people, including 13 crew – was fierce. Voyage leader Stu Hanchet says, ‘We could have filled the science positions four times over ... we had so many people requesting a berth ... We ended up with a really strong team.'

B It would be hard to overstate how hostile the Antarctic environment is for scientists. The Tangaroa's captain, Graham Leachman, explains that the Ross Sea is subject to katabatic winds* that sweep down off the Antarctic continent to create rough seas. Another danger is the possibility of the ship colliding with floating ice. ‘Even though the ship's officers use all sorts of high-tech equipment ... none of it can tell you how thick the ice is,' says Leachman, ‘and you still can't beat looking out of the window.' In the dark, he says, you can't tell how thick the ice is, but if you can see its colour, it's possible to estimate. This is why he prefers sailing in summer, when the hours of daylight in these high latitudes are longest, even though this plays tricks with his passengers' body clocks.

C Analysis of what the expedition found continues, but it's likely that several new species have been discovered and numerous other secrets revealed about life 3,000 metres below the surface. ‘We have collected huge worms and strange crustaceans,' says Livingston, 'but most impressive of all were the starfish that measured more than half a metre across – that's most abnormal for creatures belonging to this species.' This phenomenon of Antarctic seas is called 'gigantism' – the fact that some species grow to unusually large sizes. Livingston suggests various possible causes for gigantism including the extreme cold, few predators and high levels of oxygen in the seawater, but as yet no final determination can be made. Another interesting discovery was that in some places every inch of the sea floor was covered with life, whereas elsewhere icebergs have scoured out deep scars and ravines in the sea floor as they go by.

D By using deep-sea trawl nets, high-definition cameras and water samplers, the team has revealed that many of the creatures that live at extreme depths have a bizarre appearance. Among them were spotted tunicates, plankton-eating animals that are slender structures that appear to be fashioned from glass. The most fearsome-looking fish was the Southern Ocean daggertooth, a species that is ‘monocyclic', meaning the fish die after the first spawning. They are also unusual for being capable of shedding their teeth and growing a new set. Another predatory fish brought to the surface was the stareater, an extraordinary species that has an appendage like a piece of cord hanging from its chin. In these deep, dark waters, this glows red and attracts prey to swim within striking distance. Just as impressive and much more beautiful were the basket stars, a species related to starfish that lives on the seabed. The basket stars' five arms branch out numerous times to form a spectacular fan-like structure which they turn to face into the current so that food is brought into their embrace.

E But whatever exciting discoveries were made, everyday life onboard ship in the Ross Sea is unrelenting. Most people share a cabin with one other person – they're allocated so that as one person begins their 12 hours off duty, the other occupant is starting work on deck. The fresh food runs out in a few days and after that most provisions are frozen, canned or dried. Expedition general manager Fred Smits recognises that the cook has an essential role in ensuring the well-being of those onboard. ‘When you are at sea for so long,' he says, 'you think a lot about your next meal.'

F Perhaps most controversially, one of the precious berths on the Tangaroa was taken up by cameraman Max Quinn, who filmed a documentary about the voyage. Quinn's inclusion wasn't welcomed at first. ‘Scientists by nature,' Livingston says, 'tend to be camera-shy and quiet. They're not into having cameras there, so it was difficult getting everyone's permission and agreement.' But in the end Quinn fitted in very well. ‘The trick,' he says, 'is to mostly film the scientists at work, in their professional roles ... rather than eating their breakfast.' He knows when not to intrude. The documentary is a window on a trip few people get to make and also a peek into what research really looks like. 'Science,' says Livingston, ‘is intrepid, more so than people realise. It's not necessarily examining dry samples in the laboratory, but can also mean braving the elements on deck. That's what the documentary captures, the sense of real people with real lives.'

* katabatic wind: a wind caused by the local downward motion of cool air

Questions 14–17

Reading Passage 2 has six paragraphs, A–F.

Which paragraph contains the following information?

Write the correct letter, A–F, in boxes 14–17 on your answer sheet.

ABCDEF
14 details of some equipment used by the scientists
15 a description of the challenging sailing conditions in Antarctica
16 information about the composition of the scientific group
17 the identity of a potentially unpopular person on the ship

Questions 18–23

Complete the summary below.

Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.

The expedition's findings

Analysis continues of the expedition's remarkable discoveries, including a 18 very notable for its unusual width. The reasons why creatures grow so large at great depths in Antarctica may include the highly oxygenated water, the temperature, or the small number of 19 . A further fascinating finding was the existence of canyons in the seabed caused by passing 20 . Many creatures living at great depth look very strange, such as tunicates, which seem to be made of 21 . One frightening-looking fish species is characterised by loss of its 22 and the fact that it spawns only once. Another fish has something like a length of string attached to its 23 that assists with hunting.

Questions 24–26

Look at the following people (Questions 24–26) and the list of opinions below.

Match each person with the correct opinion, A–G.

24 Mary Livingston

25 Stu Hanchet

26 Max Quinn

List of opinions
A The repetitive food was one of the hardships of the voyage.
B Respecting your subjects' privacy gets the best results.
C The summer is the best time to sail these waters.
D The kitchen is one of the most important parts of the ship.

passageNotes.label: Paragraph A
passageNotes.text: 新西兰对国际极地年的贡献是“坦加罗亚”号船为期52天的航行，目的是在南极洲的罗斯海进行研究。首席科学家玛丽·利文斯顿强调这是一次多么多方面的考察，汇集了来自渔业部、国家水与大气研究所、国家博物馆和各大学的动物学家、海洋学家、气象学家和其他科学家，来研究南极洲海洋下的生命。对铺位的竞争非常激烈——该船可搭载44人，包括13名船员。航行负责人斯图·汉切特说：“我们本可以把科学职位填满四次……有那么多人申请一个铺位……我们最终组建了一支非常强大的团队。”

passageNotes.label: Paragraph B
passageNotes.text: 南极环境对科学家的恶劣程度怎么强调都不为过。“坦加罗亚”号的船长格雷厄姆·利奇曼解释说，罗斯海受到下降风的影响，这些风从南极大陆吹下来，造成汹涌的海面。另一个危险是船只与浮冰相撞的可能性。利奇曼说：“尽管船上的官员使用各种高科技设备……但没有一种能告诉你冰有多厚，你仍然不如从窗户往外看。”他说，在黑暗中，你无法判断冰有多厚，但如果你能看到它的颜色，就有可能估计出来。这就是为什么他更喜欢在夏天航行，因为在这些高纬度地区，夏天的日照时间最长，尽管这会扰乱乘客的生物钟。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph C
passageNotes.text: 对考察发现的分析仍在继续，但很可能已经发现了几个新物种，并揭示了关于海面以下3000米生命的许多其他秘密。利文斯顿说：“我们收集了巨大的蠕虫和奇怪的甲壳类动物，但最令人印象深刻的是那些直径超过半米的海星——这对于属于这个物种的生物来说是最不正常的。”南极海域的这种现象被称为“巨大化”——即某些物种长得异常大。利文斯顿提出了巨大化的各种可能原因，包括极度寒冷、捕食者少和海水中含氧量高，但目前还无法做出最终确定。另一个有趣的发现是，在某些地方，海底的每一寸都被生命覆盖，而在其他地方，冰山经过时在海底刮出了深深的伤痕和沟壑。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph D
passageNotes.text: 通过使用深海拖网、高清摄像头和水样采集器，研究小组揭示了生活在极端深度的许多生物有着奇异的外观。其中包括斑点海鞘，它们是食浮游动物的纤细结构，看起来像是由玻璃制成的。最可怕的鱼是南大洋匕齿鱼，这是一种“单周期”物种，意味着这种鱼在第一次产卵后就会死亡。它们还因为能够脱落牙齿并长出新牙齿而不寻常。另一种被带到水面的捕食性鱼是食星鱼，这是一种非凡的物种，它的下巴上挂着一根像绳子一样的附属物。在这些深邃、黑暗的水域中，它发出红色的光，吸引猎物游到攻击距离内。同样令人印象深刻且更加美丽的是篮星，这是一种与海星有关的物种，生活在海床上。篮星的五条臂多次分枝，形成壮观的扇形结构，将其转向面对水流，以便食物被带入它们的怀抱。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph E
passageNotes.text: 但无论做出了多么令人兴奋的发现，在罗斯海船上的日常生活都是艰苦的。大多数人与另一个人共用一间船舱——他们的分配方式是，当一个人开始12小时的休息时，另一个人开始在甲板上工作。新鲜食物几天就吃完了，之后大多数食物都是冷冻的、罐装的或干燥的。考察总经理弗雷德·斯密茨认识到，厨师在确保船上人员的健康方面发挥着至关重要的作用。他说：“当你在海上待了这么长时间，你会想很多关于下一顿饭的事情。”

passageNotes.label: Paragraph F
passageNotes.text: 也许最有争议的是，“坦加罗亚”号上一个宝贵的铺位被摄影师马克斯·奎因占据，他拍摄了一部关于这次航行的纪录片。奎因的加入最初并不受欢迎。利文斯顿说：“科学家天生就不喜欢上镜头，而且很安静。他们不喜欢有摄像机在那里，所以很难得到每个人的许可和同意。”但最终奎因很好地融入了团队。他说：“诀窍是主要拍摄工作中的科学家，在他们的专业角色中……而不是在吃早餐的时候。”他知道什么时候不该打扰。这部纪录片是了解一次很少有人能经历的旅程的窗口，也是对研究真正面貌的一瞥。利文斯顿说：“科学是无畏的，比人们意识到的更无畏。它不一定是在实验室里检查枯燥的样本，也可以意味着在甲板上勇敢面对恶劣天气。这就是纪录片所捕捉到的，真实的人过着真实的生活的感觉。”

items.text:
（1）题目 14：details of some equipment used by the scientists
题目翻译：科学家所用部分设备的具体信息。
答案：D
定位：正文 D 段，第1句
原文：By using deep-sea trawl nets, high-definition cameras and water samplers, the team has revealed that many of the creatures that live at extreme depths have a bizarre appearance.
译文：团队使用深海拖网、高清摄像机和取水器，揭示了许多生活在极深水域的生物外形奇特。

解析：题干强调设备的 details；D段逐项列出 deep-sea trawl nets、high-definition cameras 和 water samplers，信息最具体，因此选 D。

（2）题目 15：a description of the challenging sailing conditions in Antarctica
题目翻译：对南极艰难航行条件的描述。
答案：B
定位：正文 B 段，第1至3句
原文：the Ross Sea is subject to katabatic winds* that sweep down off the Antarctic continent to create rough seas. Another danger is the possibility of the ship colliding with floating ice.
译文：罗斯海受从南极大陆俯冲而下的下降风影响，海况恶劣；另一危险是船只可能撞上浮冰。

解析：rough seas、katabatic winds 与 floating ice 从风浪和冰况两方面说明航行挑战，因此选 B。

（3）题目 16：information about the composition of the scientific group
题目翻译：科研团队由哪些人员构成的信息。
答案：A
定位：正文 A 段，第2句
原文：bringing together zoologists, oceanographers, meteorologists and other scientists from the Ministry of Fisheries, the National Institute for Water and Atmospheric Research, the National Museum and various universities
译文：团队集合了动物学家、海洋学家、气象学家，以及来自渔业部、国家水与大气研究所、国家博物馆和多所大学的其他科学家。

解析：composition 指团队包含哪些专业与机构；A段同时列出学科和成员来源，直接对应，因此选 A。

（4）题目 17：the identity of a potentially unpopular person on the ship
题目翻译：船上一位可能不受欢迎者的身份。
答案：F
定位：正文 F 段，开头两句
原文：one of the precious berths on the Tangaroa was taken up by cameraman Max Quinn, who filmed a documentary about the voyage. Quinn’s inclusion wasn’t welcomed at first.
译文：Tangaroa号一个宝贵舱位由拍摄航程纪录片的摄影师 Max Quinn 占用；起初大家并不欢迎他的加入。

解析：potentially unpopular 对应 wasn’t welcomed at first，而人物身份明确是 cameraman Max Quinn，因此选 F。

items.text:
（1）题目 18：Analysis continues of the expedition’s remarkable discoveries, including a ________, very notable for its unusual width. The reasons why creatures grow so large at great depths in Antarctica may include the highly oxygenated water, the temperature, or the small number of ________. A further fascinating finding was the existence of canyons in the seabed caused by passing ________. Many creatures living at great depth look very strange, such as tunicates, which seem to be made of ________. One frightening-looking fish species is characterised by loss of its ________ and the fact that it spawns only once. Another fish has something like a length of string attached to its ________ that assists with hunting.
题目翻译：这些发现包括一种________，它异常宽大，十分引人注目。
答案：starfish
定位：正文 C 段，第2句
原文：most impressive of all were the starfish that measured more than half a metre across
译文：最令人印象深刻的是宽度超过半米的海星。

解析：题干的 unusual width 对应 measured more than half a metre across；空格需要这种生物的原文单词 starfish。

（2）题目 19：Analysis continues of the expedition’s remarkable discoveries, including a ________, very notable for its unusual width. The reasons why creatures grow so large at great depths in Antarctica may include the highly oxygenated water, the temperature, or the small number of ________. Many creatures living at great depth look very strange, such as tunicates, which seem to be made of ________. One frightening-looking fish species is characterised by loss of its ________ and the fact that it spawns only once. Another fish has something like a length of string attached to its ________ that assists with hunting.
题目翻译：生物巨型化的原因之一可能是________数量很少。
答案：predators
定位：正文 C 段，第4句
原文：possible causes for gigantism including the extreme cold, few predators and high levels of oxygen in the seawater
译文：巨型化的可能原因包括极端低温、捕食者很少以及海水含氧量高。

解析：题干 small number of 改写原文 few，空格应填其中心名词 predators。

（3）题目 20：Analysis continues of the expedition’s remarkable discoveries, including a ________, very notable for its unusual width. The reasons why creatures grow so large at great depths in Antarctica may include the highly oxygenated water, the temperature, or the small number of ________. A further fascinating finding was the existence of canyons in the seabed caused by passing ________. Many creatures living at great depth look very strange, such as tunicates, which seem to be made of ________. One frightening-looking fish species is characterised by loss of its ________ and the fact that it spawns only once. Another fish has something like a length of string attached to its ________ that assists with hunting.
题目翻译：海床中的峡谷由经过的________造成。
答案：icebergs
定位：正文 C 段，末句
原文：icebergs have scoured out deep scars and ravines in the sea floor as they go by
译文：冰山经过时在海床上刮出深深的痕迹和沟谷。

解析：canyons 对应 ravines，passing 对应 as they go by；造成这些海床痕迹的是 icebergs。

（4）题目 21：Analysis continues of the expedition’s remarkable discoveries, including a ________, very notable for its unusual width. Another fish has something like a length of string attached to its ________ that assists with hunting.
题目翻译：海鞘看起来像是由________制成。
答案：glass
定位：正文 D 段，第2句
原文：spotted tunicates, plankton-eating animals that are slender structures that appear to be fashioned from glass
译文：斑点海鞘是以浮游生物为食的细长动物，看起来仿佛由玻璃制成。

解析：seem to be made of 是 appear to be fashioned from 的同义改写，后接原词 glass。

答案：chin

原文：the stareater, an extraordinary species that has an appendage like a piece of cord hanging from its chin. In these deep, dark waters, this glows red and attracts prey
译文：食星鱼有一个像细绳般从下巴垂下的附器；在深暗水域中它发出红光吸引猎物。

One frightening-looking fish species is characterised by loss of its ________ and the fact that it spawns only once. Another fish has something like a length of string attached to its ________ that assists with hunting.
题目翻译：这些发现包括一种________，它异常宽大，十分引人注目。
答案：starfish
定位：正文 C 段，第2句
原文：most impressive of all were the starfish that measured more than half a metre across
译文：最令人印象深刻的是宽度超过半米的海星。

解析：题干的 unusual width 对应 measured more than half a metre across；空格需要这种生物的原文单词 starfish。

（2）题目 19：Analysis continues of the expedition’s remarkable discoveries, including a ________, very notable for its unusual width. The reasons why creatures grow so large at great depths in Antarctica may include the highly oxygenated water, the temperature, or the small number of ________. A further fascinating finding was the existence of canyons in the seabed caused by passing ________. Many creatures living at great depth look very strange, such as tunicates, which seem to be made of ________. One frightening-looking fish species is characterised by loss of its ________ and the fact that it spawns only once. Another fish has something like a length of string attached to its ________ that assists with hunting.
题目翻译：生物巨型化的原因之一可能是________数量很少。
答案：predators
定位：正文 C 段，第4句
原文：possible causes for gigantism including the extreme cold, few predators and high levels of oxygen in the seawater
译文：巨型化的可能原因包括极端低温、捕食者很少以及海水含氧量高。

解析：题干 small number of 改写原文 few，空格应填其中心名词 predators。

（3）题目 20：Analysis continues of the expedition’s remarkable discoveries, including a ________, very notable for its unusual width. The reasons why creatures grow so large at great depths in Antarctica may include the highly oxygenated water, the temperature, or the small number of ________. A further fascinating finding was the existence of canyons in the seabed caused by passing ________. Many creatures living at great depth look very strange, such as tunicates, which seem to be made of ________. One frightening-looking fish species is characterised by loss of its ________ and the fact that it spawns only once. Another fish has something like a length of string attached to its ________ that assists with hunting.
题目翻译：海床中的峡谷由经过的________造成。
答案：icebergs
定位：正文 C 段，末句
原文：icebergs have scoured out deep scars and ravines in the sea floor as they go by
译文：冰山经过时在海床上刮出深深的痕迹和沟谷。

解析：canyons 对应 ravines，passing 对应 as they go by；造成这些海床痕迹的是 icebergs。

（4）题目 21：Analysis continues of the expedition’s remarkable discoveries, including a ________, very notable for its unusual width. The reasons why creatures grow so large at great depths in Antarctica may include the highly oxygenated water, the temperature, or the small number of ________. A further fascinating finding was the existence of canyons in the seabed caused by passing ________. Many creatures living at great depth look very strange, such as tunicates, which seem to be made of ________. One frightening-looking fish species is characterised by loss of its ________ and the fact that it spawns only once. Another fish has something like a length of string attached to its ________ that assists with hunting.
题目翻译：海鞘看起来像是由________制成。
答案：glass
定位：正文 D 段，第2句
原文：spotted tunicates, plankton-eating animals that are slender structures that appear to be fashioned from glass
译文：斑点海鞘是以浮游生物为食的细长动物，看起来仿佛由玻璃制成。

解析：seem to be made of 是 appear to be fashioned from 的同义改写，后接原词 glass。

（5）题目 22：Analysis continues of the expedition’s remarkable discoveries, including a ________, very notable for its unusual width. The reasons why creatures grow so large at great depths in Antarctica may include the highly oxygenated water, the temperature, or the small number of ________. A further fascinating finding was the existence of canyons in the seabed caused by passing ________. Many creatures living at great depth look very strange, such as tunicates, which seem to be made of ________. One frightening-looking fish species is characterised by loss of its ________ and the fact that it spawns only once. Another fish has something like a length of string attached to its ________ that assists with hunting.
题目翻译：这种可怕外形的鱼会失去自己的________，而且只繁殖一次。
答案：teeth
定位：正文 D 段，第3至4句
原文：meaning the fish die after the first spawning. They are also unusual for being capable of shedding their teeth
译文：这种鱼首次产卵后便死亡，而且还能脱落自己的牙齿。

解析：spawns only once 对应 first spawning，loss of 对应 shedding；被脱落的是 teeth。

（6）题目 23：Analysis continues of the expedition’s remarkable discoveries, including a ________, very notable for its unusual width. The reasons why creatures grow so large at great depths in Antarctica may include the highly oxygenated water, the temperature, or the small number of ________. A further fascinating finding was the existence of canyons in the seabed caused by passing ________. Many creatures living at great depth look very strange, such as tunicates, which seem to be made of ________. One frightening-looking fish species is characterised by loss of its ________ and the fact that it spawns only once. Another fish has something like a length of string attached to its ________ that assists with hunting.
题目翻译：另一种鱼有一条像绳子的东西连在它的________上，帮助捕猎。
答案：chin
定位：正文 D 段，第5至6句
原文：the stareater, an extraordinary species that has an appendage like a piece of cord hanging from its chin. In these deep, dark waters, this glows red and attracts prey
译文：食星鱼有一个像细绳般从下巴垂下的附器；在深暗水域中它发出红光吸引猎物。

解析：a length of string 对应 a piece of cord，attached to 对应 hanging from；附器连接在 chin。

items.text:
（1）题目 24：Mary Livingston
题目翻译：科学工作的性质可能令一些人感到意外。
答案：F
定位：正文 F 段，末三句
原文：Science,’ says Livingston, ‘is intrepid, more so than people realise. It’s not necessarily examining dry samples in the laboratory, but can also mean braving the elements on deck.
译文：Livingston说，科学比人们以为的更勇于冒险；它不只是研究实验室里的干燥样本，也可能意味着在甲板上迎战恶劣天气。

解析：她强调科学工作的真实面貌比大众想象的更勇敢、更出人意料，对应 F。

（2）题目 25：Stu Hanchet
题目翻译：报名参加该团队的人数超过了可提供的名额。
答案：G
定位：正文 A 段，末两句
原文：We could have filled the science positions four times over … we had so many people requesting a berth
译文：科研岗位足以招满四遍，因为申请舱位的人非常多。

解析：申请人数远超岗位数量，直接对应 G“申请多于名额”。

（3）题目 26：Max Quinn
题目翻译：尊重研究对象的隐私能获得最佳结果。
答案：B
定位：正文 F 段，中部 Quinn 的引语及下一句
原文：The trick,’ he says, ‘is to mostly film the scientists at work, in their professional roles … rather than eating their breakfast.’ He knows when not to intrude.
译文：诀窍是主要拍摄科学家工作时的专业状态，而不是他们吃早餐时；他知道什么时候不该打扰。

解析：选择专业工作场景并懂得不介入，体现尊重被拍者隐私才能得到最佳效果，对应 B。
